A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same numerical evidence extraction and study-level inference system. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, input and training ablations, and manual analyses of model-generated reasoning in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports training reward trajectories in Figure 3.

M1.justification: The extraction-plus-effect-estimation pipeline, SFT and GRPO training, output schema, and three rewards with weights 0.8/0.1/0.1 are retained. V2's expanded policy notation does not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCHRANE FOREST EXT for training and COCHRANE FOREST and the Yun et al. RCT dataset for evaluation, covering the same binary and continuous outcome tasks. The added reward analysis introduces no new dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 2 retains the GPT-4, Qwen2.5, Llama-3.1, and DeepSeek-Qwen baselines; Table 3 retains URCA and GraphRAG; Table 4 retains SFT-no-CoT and RL-EX. Newly discussed related work is not experimentally added.

E3.justification: The 1,864/208 training-validation split, 725 and 413 evaluation instances, metrics, model sizes, zero-shot comparisons, and training budgets remain unchanged. Figure 3 examines existing RL training without specifying a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds a reward-dynamics analysis comparing how quickly format and numerical-correctness rewards develop during training. Existing input ablations, CoT and reward ablations, manual reasoning analysis, and the appendix case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed benchmark estimates, confidence intervals for model performance, or significance tests. Clinical effect confidence intervals and Appendix C's annotation-agreement reporting are unchanged; the new reward plot adds no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the RCT exact-match gain from 21.2 to 20.9 points, consistent with the unchanged Table 2 values of 41.2 and 20.3. Figure 3 newly reports early format-reward plateaus and slower correctness-reward gains. Benchmark and ablation table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds the normalization index range j in {i,...,G}, absent in v1, creating an inconsistency with the accompanying whole-group mean and variance description. Its explicit current/old-policy probability ratio otherwise clarifies GRPO. The reward equations, effect-size mathematics, and Appendix A derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and headline performance claims remain essentially unchanged. Section 5 adds an explicit claim to be the first to apply RL specifically to numerical evidence extraction from biomedical studies for systematic reviews, strengthening the novelty claim.

C2.justification: V2 interprets reward trajectories as learning output structure before numerical correctness. Section 7 changes the evidence requirement from explicitly reported to explicitly or implicitly reported and removes indirect reporting from its failure list, consistent with the retained case study. The conclusion adds prospective clinical decision-support and cross-domain applications.

D1.justification: The prompts, annotation instructions, hyperparameters, gradient accumulation, eight 80GB A100 GPUs, Open-R1 and vLLM software, API usage, and licensing/access information are retained in Section 4.1 and Appendices B–F. No new implementation settings or code/data availability are reported.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially expands research positioning through comparisons with Wang, Lai, and Sun on clinical extraction, a new RL-focused discussion including Lin's EHR reasoning work, and links to argument mining and AI for Science. It adds an explicit priority claim, extending well beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V2 expands RL in the title, clarifies GRPO exposition, adds localized analysis and related-work paragraphs, and extends the conclusion. The overall section sequence and most existing prose, including appendix explanations, remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds reward-dynamics Figure 3, redraws the retrieval-performance Figure 2, simplifies table rules, and changes some float placement. V1 Figures 3–8 are retained as v2 Figures 4–9, including identical appendix images; the overall two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: The new training diagnostic, broader clinical-extraction and RL context, corrected EM-gain arithmetic, and better-aligned limitation modestly improve explanation and reporting. These benefits are limited by unchanged benchmark evidence and a new indexing inconsistency in the GRPO normalization formula. The revision improves the paper without substantially strengthening its empirical foundation.
